scenario: [LEXP.6.2] `len` of a Json value that is not an array is a TypeError ([LEXP.7.12.1]), which abandons the activation, so the rule does not fire. Two dead rules for the two non-array shapes the clause covers — an object and a scalar — plus a live control over a real array, without which a `len` that faulted on EVERYTHING would pass the dead pair and pin nothing. Each runtime reaches the node through the root and the path (DS_FN_JSON_LEN), not through the projected value, in which an object, an array and a string are one String. The unresolved-path case rides the same arm and is not separately driven: [LNUL.8.4] makes it `null`, which is not an array either.
rules_ds:
schema Payload scope logical:
    body: Json key

rule len_of_an_object_is_a_type_error:
    Payload p where len(p.body.obj) == 1
->
    log critical "len-obj"

rule len_of_a_scalar_is_a_type_error:
    Payload p where len(p.body.scalar) == 2
->
    log critical "len-scalar"

rule len_of_the_array_still_answers:
    Payload p where len(p.body.arr) == 2
->
    log critical "len-arr"
